findings.title: Word-hint requests have no raw utility byte admission
findings.expected: An outside utility request has an explicit size bound; reuse the existing InputText domain, preserving normal last-word behavior. This is a coding-rule bound, not an altered cryptographic-format requirement.
findings.observed: Both actual raw bindings and public classes accept8193UTF8bytes for bothbip39/eff lists; all8192positives also pass. ASCII and multibyte whitespace show bytes, not character counts. Class transport includes the whole supplied payload.
findings.impact: Avoidable linear scanning and copied/transferred data before a small answer; no measured exhaustion, remote attack or secret leak. Native typed-line front ends already cap their input; raw/browser callers expose this gap.
findings.recommendedFix: Settle the public hint input contract and use library-owned admission in the raw binding and pre-encode class paths; expose/reuse needed metadata. Do not silently truncate text or alter KDF parameters.
findings.requiredVerification: Exact max/max+1 byte controls with multibyte input; normal hints/completions; stable error code; pre-copy/worker ordering; document any source API signature/limit changes.

findings.title: Invalid UTF-8 in an interactive visible answer bypasses retry
findings.expected: Explain the invalid interactive answer and ask the same field again, preserving preceding answers. Real I/O failure and cancellation remain failures/stops.
findings.observed: The ordinary malformed fingerprint is asked again, but the invalid UTF-8 answer ends the process with exit code 2.
findings.impact: Recoverable interactive input loses prior state. Script fail-fast behavior is not alleged to be wrong; hidden secret input has a separate retry loop.
findings.recommendedFix: Handle the existing typed invalid-input refusal at the interactive visible-input seam and drain only the refused line; do not swallow cancellation or genuine I/O errors.
findings.requiredVerification: The actual PTY control remains alive and re-prompts after malformed UTF-8, accepts a subsequent valid answer, preserves prior state, and keeps script exits/cancellation/I/O semantics.
findings.reproduction: At the actual current check --fingerprint interactive prompt, first enter an ordinary invalid fingerprint and observe a new prompt; then submit byte FF followed by LF.

findings.title: An excessive interactive BIP39 passphrase is refused only after its prompt
findings.expected: The passphrase's shared raw-byte domain is applied at the interactive prompt and an invalid value is asked again without retyping earlier answers.
findings.observed: The prompt accepts the line; later reference preflight refuses it with the correct passphrase-size error and the process exits 2. No recovery round runs.
findings.impact: Late recoverable input refusal loses prior interactive state. This is not the historical too-late-KDF variant: the native domain guard correctly prevents Argon2 rounds.
findings.recommendedFix: Expose/reuse the existing library-owned passphrase size rule in the shared CLI passphrase reader, preserving empty-passphrase applicability and script refusal behavior.
findings.requiredVerification: 1024/1025 raw bytes, multibyte byte counts, retry preserving earlier answers, named/nonempty and optional-empty prompts, scripts and no work before refusal.
findings.reproduction: Supply the published zero-12 container, synthetic password and valid fingerprint to actual check --fingerprint; submit a synthetic 1025-byte ASCII BIP39 passphrase.

findings.title: Follow-up: CLI self-test source comment still overstates finite coverage
findings.reproduction: Compare the actual CLI header comment at6-9 with the limited library self-test evidence and implementation; no full-cost execution is required to establish a wording mismatch.
findings.expected: Passing published checks establishes only the tested operations and witnessed rounds, not all MHFE inputs here and now.
findings.observed: The comment still says a passing program computes MHFE as the specification says here and now; the library correctly limits evidence to two published operations and their witnessed rounds.
findings.impact: Limited source documentation overclaim, not an altered runtime verdict or a new cryptographic vulnerability.
findings.recommendedFix: Qualify the current CLI source comment to the actual finite checks, retaining the original finding ID.
findings.requiredVerification: Source/wording comparison against the library; no new full-cost campaign merely for a comment.
